title: Evaluation-defined constructible Verdier duality through coefficients
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\ge1$. Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. All schemes below are separated of finite type over $k$ and all morphisms are separated of finite type. At $A_n$ write $\mathcal C_{T,A_n}=D^b_{ctf}(T,A_n)$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor category; at $R,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ write $\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda}=D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$. Integral categories use completed coefficient sheaves and derived completeness with reductions in one finite cohomological interval independent of $n$; field categories use rationalization and common finite coefficient-field stages, respectively. 

Let $f:X\to Y$, let $a_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure map, and set $\omega_T=Ra_T^!\Lambda$, $D_T=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_T)$. For $M\in\mathcal C_{X,\Lambda}$, the evaluation-defined constructible Verdier exchange is a natural isomorphism
$$D_YRf_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*D_XM.$$
At finite stages it is the constructible formal exchange for finite-Tor $M$, with its shift and coefficient comparisons. At each $A_n$, $D_T:\mathcal C_{T,A_n}^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq\mathcal C_{T,A_n}$ is an exact anti-equivalence and the tensor--Hom transpose of evaluation $\delta_M:M\to D_TD_TM$ is its natural biduality isomorphism. For every locally closed piece $T\subseteq Y$, every closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ between such pieces, and every $L\in\mathcal C_{T,A_n}$, the canonical evaluation-defined boundary comparisons $i^*D_TL\to D_ZRi^!L$ of [def-weil-boundary-duality-input] are isomorphisms, as consequences of this geometric duality rather than hypotheses on it.
At $R$, bounded constructibility agrees with the uniform finite-Tor constructible domain. Verdier duality preserves it with uniform dimension-dependent output bounds. Its finite reductions, evaluations and $\delta$ are the evaluation-defined comparisons of the integral construction. Rationalization gives an $E$-linear exact anti-equivalence with those same rationalized evaluation and biduality maps. Finite coefficient-field extension and retract descent give an exact anti-equivalence at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with these common-stage evaluation and biduality maps. Thus at all three higher stages $D_T:\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda}^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda}$ and $\delta:\mathrm{id}\simeq D_TD_T$ are the actual coefficient-passage maps. These claims use the constructible exceptional functor only.

proof.text: Fix a scheme $T$ and a finite level $A_n$ from the statement. Its separated finite-type hypothesis and $\ell\ne p$ are exactly the hypotheses of [thm-fix-general-biduality]. On the small pro-etale site that theorem makes $D_T=R\mathcal Hom(-,Ra_T^!A_n)$ an exact anti-equivalence of $D^b_{ctf}(T,A_n)$ and makes $\delta_M$ a natural isomorphism. The map denoted $\delta$ here is the transpose of evaluation in [lem-weil-duality-pairing]; exchanging the two tensor factors uses the tensor symmetry. Thus this proves the finite-stage clause for the specified evaluation map, without a boundary-duality hypothesis.

source.place: Finite-stage geometric biduality and its evaluation-compatible pro-etale transport

proof.text: Apply [cor-weil-boundary-duality-discharge] to the given $Y$ and $A_n$. Its conclusion quantifies over every locally closed piece $T$ and closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ occurring in [def-weil-boundary-duality-input], so it applies to precisely the $i$ and $L$ in the item. It asserts invertibility of the canonical $\beta_L$, not just existence of some isomorphism between its source and target. In the cited definition $\beta_L$ is the transpose of the displayed pairing $i^*D_TL\otimes^LRi^!L\to Ri^!(D_TL\otimes^LL)\to\omega_Z$. Hence it is the evaluation-defined boundary comparison required here. The corollary discharges the entire boundary input after geometric biduality; that input was not assumed in step 1.

source.place: Boundary input discharged after biduality; identification of beta by evaluation

proof.text: At $R$, [prop-coef-integral-dualizing] identifies the derived-complete object $\omega_{T,R}$ used in [thm-coef-integral-verdier] with the value of the constructible exceptional right adjoint at the coefficient unit, so it is the $Ra_T^!R$ of this item. Apply the integral theorem on exactly its completed coefficient-sheaf category. It gives $D^b_c(T,R)=D^b_{ctf}(T,R)$ and an exact anti-equivalence for the actual internal Hom into this $\omega_{T,R}$. If $\dim T\le d$ and the input reductions have common Tor interval $[a,b]$, its output reductions have common interval $[-b-2d,-a]$. Its canonical reduction maps identify $(D_{T,R}M)\otimes_R^LA_n$ with $D_{T,n}M_n$, preserve evaluation and its transposes, and identify the reduction of the actual $\delta_M$ with $\delta_{M_n}$. The same theorem asserts that this natural $\delta_M$ is invertible. These are exactly the integral preservation, bounds and coefficient-map assertions; no independent choice of double-dual isomorphism is made.

source.place: Integral preservation and uniform interval; reduction of actual evaluation and double dual; with prop-coef-integral-dualizing value-at-unit assertion

proof.text: Apply [thm-coef-rational-verdier] to $T$ and the given finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. It gives the exact $E$-linear anti-equivalence on the specified rationalization of $D^b_c(T,R)$, with evaluation and the natural invertible $\delta$ obtained by rationalizing their integral maps. By [lem-coef-rational-operations], its dual is $R\mathcal Hom_E(-,\omega_{T,E})$ and $\omega_{T,E}=Ra_{T,E}^!E$, with these identifications preserving evaluations. Thus the anti-equivalence is the $D_T$ in the item. For every finite $E\subset L$, the comparison in the rational theorem preserves evaluation and $\delta$ and satisfies the scalar-extension unit and associator equations. This supplies the coherent comparisons used at a common field stage in the next step.

source.place: Rationalize integral duality and its actual maps; finite coefficient-field comparisons

proof.text: For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, apply [thm-coef-qbar-verdier] on the common finite coefficient-field category specified in the item. It sends a representative $(E,M)$ to $(E,D_{T,E}M)$ and asserts that the resulting exact anti-equivalence is internal Hom into $Ra_T^!\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Its descended evaluation and biduality are therefore the common-stage maps required here. Its statement includes compatibility with finite scalar extension and retracts, so the same conclusion holds for objects and maps represented as retracts at a common finite stage. In particular the descended $\delta$ is a natural isomorphism on the entire stated category, not merely on a separately selected collection of representatives.

source.place: Common-stage descent of duals, evaluation and biduality, including retracts

proof.text: The exchange theorem below has input $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. At $A_n$ this is precisely $\mathcal C_{X,A_n}$. At $R$ step 3 proved that it is all of $\mathcal C_{X,R}$. At $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] defines the finite-Tor categories to equal the rationalized and common-stage bounded constructible categories. Thus every $M$ allowed by this item lies in the stated domain of that theorem. This does not identify arbitrary bounded constructible finite-ring complexes with finite-Tor ones.

source.place: For (7): coefficient domains for the exchange; field finite-Tor convention

proof.text: Use [sk-thm-sf-verdier-exchange] for $f:X\to Y$ and the $M$ just checked. It uses the constructible exceptional adjoint, has no ambient admissibility hypothesis, and gives the canonical comparison $c:Rf^!\omega_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_X$ and the natural isomorphism $\varepsilon_{f,M}:D_YRf_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*D_XM$ at all four stages. In the normalization of [def-sf-verdier-exchange-data], this is the arrow obtained from projection and evaluation by the exceptional, tensor--Hom and ordinary adjunctions and then substitution of $c$. Equivalently it is the inverse tensor--Hom exchange followed by $Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_X(M,c)$. This identifies the canonical map, rather than replacing it by an arbitrary isomorphism. The theorem explicitly supplies finite reduction, scalar extension and shift compatibility on the stated domains, with completed integral and rationalized/common-stage field comparisons. Together with steps 1--5 this proves every clause of the item, using only the constructible exceptional functor.

source.place: Steps 1--2 and final compatibility sentence, with the canonical evaluation normalization
